section_summary: This section follows Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation’s Japanese trademark disputes over GTD and OTD marks. It records the invalidation of S. Nakagawa’s GTD registration, the subsequent rejection of Greenfield’s own application, and correspondence with the State Department and American Embassy about the next steps.

subfiles.title: Notice of opposition to OTD registration
subfiles.about: Counsel reports opposition to Japanese OTD registration No. 10260 based on Greenfield’s earlier registrations.
subfiles.summary: Opposition was entered against OTD in Class 17; counsel promises further news.

subfiles.title: Status of OTD opposition
subfiles.about: Japanese officials had taken no action on Greenfield’s opposition to OTD.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese associate reported no official action as of August 27.

subfiles.title: Refusal of opposition to OTD
subfiles.about: Counsel reports that Japanese authorities rejected Greenfield’s opposition to OTD.
subfiles.summary: The decision found OTD distinguishable from Greenfield’s GTD marks in sound and appearance. Counsel sharply disputes that reasoning.

subfiles.title: Greenfield response to OTD refusal
subfiles.about: Greenfield questions the consistency of Japanese trademark reasoning and suggests approaching the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Greenfield asks whether the OTD ruling should be referred to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of counsel’s January correspondence
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges letters on Greenfield’s Japanese trademark protection.
subfiles.summary: Copies of the January 6 and 7 letters and enclosures are being sent to Ambassador Grew.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Greenfield correspondence to Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department forwards counsel’s January letters concerning Greenfield’s trademark protection in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy receives copies of two letters and enclosures for information.

subfiles.title: Greenfield reports successful GTD invalidation
subfiles.about: Greenfield reports cancellation of a Japanese registration for its GTD mark.
subfiles.summary: Greenfield thanks the Department and says it will proceed with renewal of its own registration.

subfiles.title: Muller, Phipps & Sellers reports invalidation
subfiles.about: The firm reports success in invalidating S. Nakagawa’s GTD registration.
subfiles.summary: Copies of the Japanese attorneys’ correspondence are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Japanese attorneys report invalidation victory
subfiles.about: The attorneys report that Greenfield won its suit against registration No. 212580.
subfiles.summary: An English translation of the decision is enclosed.

subfiles.title: Decision invalidating registration No. 212580
subfiles.to: Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation and S. Nakagawa
subfiles.about: The Patent Office invalidates Nakagawa’s GTD registration as confusingly similar to Greenfield’s earlier mark.
subfiles.summary: The decision finds the marks share the sound and idea GTD and cover the same goods.

subfiles.title: State Department transmits invalidation news
subfiles.about: The Department sends the Embassy Greenfield’s report and enclosures concerning its successful invalidation suit.
subfiles.summary: The instruction highlights the ruling against S. Nakagawa’s registration.

subfiles.title: Greenfield requests Embassy help after application rejection
subfiles.about: Greenfield asks that the Embassy review rejection of its GTD application No. 19741.
subfiles.summary: Two copies of the letter report the Appeal Board’s rejection and enclose counsel’s May 24 explanation.

subfiles.title: Counsel explains rejection of GTD application
subfiles.about: Counsel explains why the Appeal Board upheld rejection despite Greenfield’s successful invalidation suit.
subfiles.summary: The invalidation of registration No. 212580 had not become final when the Appeal Board ruled. Japanese associates considered a further appeal unlikely to succeed. Counsel recommends filing a new Class 17 application once invalidation is final.

subfiles.title: Appeal decision rejecting application No. 19741
subfiles.about: The Appeal Board rejects Greenfield’s GTD panel and name application because registration No. 212580 remains on the register.
subfiles.summary: The Board finds the marks similar in sound and idea and covering the same Class 17 goods. It says Greenfield’s earlier registrations do not overcome the cited registration and declines to consider its recent protest.

subfiles.title: Greenfield requests refiling and possible appeal
subfiles.about: Greenfield instructs counsel to file a new GTD application and considers appealing the rejection.
subfiles.summary: It proposes an appeal to protect its position while the new application proceeds.

subfiles.title: State Department forwards application rejection correspondence
subfiles.about: The Department sends Greenfield’s May 29 letter and enclosure to the Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The papers concern rejection of the GTD panel and name application.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Greenfield
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Greenfield’s letter about the rejected GTD application.
subfiles.summary: A copy and enclosure have been sent to Ambassador Grew.

subfiles.title: Embassy assessment of Greenfield trademark case
subfiles.about: The Embassy evaluates the Appeal Board ruling and suggests ways to obtain Greenfield’s GTD registration.
subfiles.summary: Local contacts considered the ruling arbitrary but saw little recourse short of appeal. They advised refiling immediately or when renewing registration No. 132212. The Embassy avoided a formal approach through the Foreign Office because it might prejudice future applications.

subfiles.title: Embassy advice forwarded to Greenfield
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department sends Greenfield a copy of the Embassy’s suggestions on application No. 19741.
subfiles.summary: The date is established by Greenfield’s reply on page 185.

subfiles.title: Greenfield accepts Embassy suggestions
subfiles.from: H. M. Hubbard, Greenfield Tap and Die Corporation
subfiles.about: Greenfield thanks the Department and says it is acting on Ambassador Grew’s suggestions.
subfiles.summary: The firm expresses appreciation for State Department assistance.
